standard.title: Interpret and translate across cultural contexts
standard.description: interpret and translate non-verbal, spoken and written language to convey meaning in a range of familiar and unfamiliar cultural contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply strategies to interpret and translate language in cultural contexts, evaluate translation tools, and produce bilingual resources (AC9LCH6C04). They have managed idiom and literal translation risk. They have not yet interpreted for real visitors, converted register across formal and informal contexts, identified translation challenges involving cultural concepts, or composed bilingual texts for public or professional audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret and translate non-verbal, spoken and written language across familiar and unfamiliar cultural contexts — including register conversion, real or simulated interpreting, identifying challenges of cultural concept translation, and producing bilingual texts for public purposes.

nodes.label: Register conversion and cultural concept challenges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can convert language between formal and informal registers for different purposes, and identify and manage the challenges of translating culturally-specific concepts.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert at least one informal spoken expression into formal written register for a specific purpose, and identify at least two cultural concepts that present translation challenges, explaining why.
nodes.typical_width: Convert informal spoken language into formal register for different purposes and audiences; identify concepts that are culturally-specific and resist direct translation; develop strategies for handling these challenges; use dictionaries to understand subtle word use differences; reflect on which words and gestures should or should not be used across cultural contexts.
wider: Translate a formal public text into an accessible version for a target language community audience — documenting each register or cultural concept decision
Research a specific cultural concept that challenges translation — explain the concept in depth in English and discuss multiple strategies for conveying it to a non-target-language audience
nodes.hinge_reason: Register conversion and cultural concept handling are the prerequisites for professional-level translation and interpreting work. Students who cannot manage these challenges cannot produce contextually appropriate translations in unfamiliar contexts — the core demand of this descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Register conversion and cultural concept challenges require systematic analysis of the source text's cultural and contextual demands before translation choices are made. Explicit translation strategy instruction — with documented decision-making — builds the analytical capacity for complex translation tasks.

success_criteria: Converts at least one informal expression into formal register appropriately for a specified purpose
Identifies at least two cultural concepts that present translation challenges and explains why

nodes.label: Interpreting for real or simulated audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret between target language and English in a real or simulated context — applying clarification, rephrasing and cultural explanation strategies.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least one exchange between a target language speaker and an English speaker (real or simulated), demonstrating at least one clarification or cultural explanation strategy.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret for visitors or in simulated interpreting scenarios; apply clarification and rephrasing strategies; explain cultural concepts to English-speaking audiences; compare language and behaviour choices when communicating across cultural contexts; discuss modifications made and why.
wider: Interpret in a complex simulated scenario where a cultural misunderstanding must be identified and resolved — document the interpreting decisions made
Compare the challenges of interpreting spoken language with translating written text — identify specific differences in how real-time interpreting demands differ from text translation

response_modes.reason: Interpreting competence requires practice across varied cultural contexts and audience combinations. The same cultural concept explanation needed for one audience may not serve another; varied interpreting scenarios build flexible, audience-aware mediation capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Interpreting is an authentic real-world use of bilingual competence that background language learners may already practise in family and community contexts. Width investment here formalises and extends this capability — building the conscious strategies that transform informal bilingual practice into skilled interpreting.
success_criteria: Interprets at least one exchange demonstrating accurate meaning transfer
Uses at least one clarification or cultural explanation strategy during the interpreting task

nodes.label: Bilingual text production for public purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compose bilingual texts — menus, signs, public notices, community resources — that accurately convey meaning for both target language and English-speaking audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose at least one bilingual text for a real or realistic public purpose, demonstrating accurate meaning transfer and appropriate language conventions in both languages.
nodes.typical_width: Compose bilingual texts for public purposes — menus, signs, notices, community resources, travel itineraries; develop glossaries to accompany English texts; identify and correct translation errors in existing public signs; apply bilingual literacy for real community audiences.
wider: Identify and amend an inaccurate or culturally inappropriate public translation — explain what the error was, why it occurred, and what a correct translation would be
Create a bilingual community resource with a real community stakeholder — negotiating content and language choices for a dual-language audience

response_modes.reason: Bilingual text production integrates register conversion (node 1) and interpreting strategy (node 2) into a public-facing communicative act. The teaching investment is in creating real or realistic public audience conditions — where the text will actually be read by a dual-language audience.

success_criteria: Composes a bilingual text with accurate meaning transfer in both languages
Demonstrates appropriate language conventions for a public audience in both languages
